haiku-low.q1: They do not differ. Both get the same status, body and headers, 401 "Invalid email or password", and a dummy hash keeps timing close.
haiku-low.q2: It gets 429 with Retry-After in seconds and "Too many failed attempts. Try again later." The password is not checked and nothing is counted.
haiku-low.q3: The session that this browser's cookie points to is deleted and replaced by a new session. Sessions on other devices stay valid.
haiku-low.q4: The cookie __Host-sid holds only the opaque random session ID. It is HttpOnly, so page scripts cannot read it.
haiku-low.q5: It stops working 12 hours after login. The absolute lifetime never moves, even with constant activity. Idle timeout alone would be 30 minutes.
haiku-low.q6: It redirects to /login and clears the cookie. If the database check itself fails, it returns 503 and keeps the cookie.
haiku-low.q7: After checking the CSRF token, it deletes that session row before replying, then redirects to /login and clears the cookie. If already gone, the reply is the same.
haiku-low.q8: Session state lives in the shared Postgres sessions table, storing only the SHA-256 hash of the ID. Every instance queries that same database, so any instance finds it.
haiku-low.q9: In a login_failures row per email in Postgres. A failure restarts the count at 1 if the window started 10 or more minutes ago; otherwise it adds 1.
haiku-low.q10: It compares the cookie's hash to a session row with last_seen_at within 30 minutes and absolute_expires_at in the future. It then sets last_seen_at to now.
haiku-low.q11: 503 with the same login page and no cookie. The transaction rolls back, so the failure count is untouched.
haiku-low.q12: A background cleanup job on each instance, every 15 minutes, deletes up to 1000 expired rows per table per run.

sonnet.q1: They do not differ. Same 401 status, body ("Invalid email or password") and headers; a dummy hash keeps timing similar, and a failure row is kept for unknown emails too.
sonnet.q2: If the email is locked (locked_until in the future), the server returns 429 with Retry-After in seconds and the message "Too many failed attempts. Try again later." The password is not checked, even if correct, and the attempt changes nothing. (Caveat: the lock is set 15 minutes ahead on the 5th failure, so it applies while locked_until is still in the future.)
sonnet.q3: On successful login, the session that the browser's cookie points to is deleted (if a cookie was sent), and a new session with a new random ID is inserted. Sessions on other devices stay valid.
sonnet.q4: Only the random opaque session ID (32 random bytes, base64url). Page scripts cannot read it because the cookie is HttpOnly.
sonnet.q5: After 12 hours from login (absolute lifetime, which never moves), even with continuous activity. The idle timer of 30 minutes keeps resetting but doesn't extend the 12-hour limit.
sonnet.q6: No row comes back, so it redirects (302) to /login and clears the cookie.
sonnet.q7: After checking the CSRF token, if a cookie is present, it deletes that session row from the database before replying, then redirects to /login and clears the cookie. If the session is already gone (0 rows deleted), the reply is the same redirect and cookie clear. A database error gives 503 with cookie kept.
sonnet.q8: In the shared Postgres database, in the sessions table (also login_failures). Any instance hashes the cookie's session ID (SHA-256) and looks up id_hash in Postgres with a single statement, so no sticky sessions are needed.
sonnet.q9: In the login_failures table in Postgres, one row per email (trimmed, lowercased). The row has window_started_at; a later failure restarts the count at 1 if the window started 10 or more minutes ago (using the database clock), otherwise adds 1. The window is fixed, starting at the first failure.
sonnet.q10: It compares last_seen_at (must be within the last 30 minutes) and absolute_expires_at (must be in the future) against the database clock now(), matching by id_hash of the cookie. On a match it sets last_seen_at to now() and returns user_id.
sonnet.q11: A 503 response showing the same login page, with no cookie set. The transaction is rolled back, so the failure count is untouched.
sonnet.q12: The background cleanup job, which runs on every instance every 15 minutes. It deletes sessions where absolute_expires_at < now() or last_seen_at < now() - 30 min, at most 1000 rows per table per run.
